issue_context.title: BUG: Calling to_html with float_format strips all trailing zeros if an integer string is returned from the formatter
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas. - [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas. --- #### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example ```python import pandas as pd df = pd.DataFrame(data={'x': [1000.0, 'test']}) # Column dtype must be object df.to_html(float_format=lambda x: '{:,.0f}'.format(x)) ``` #### Output: ```html '\n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n
x
01,
1test
' ``` #### Problem description This caused by the rstrip in pandas.io.formats.format._trim_zeros_single_float() #### Expected Output ```html '\n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n
x
01,000
1test
' ``` #### Output of ``pd.show_versions()``
``` INSTALLED VERSIONS ------------------ pandas : 1.2.2 numpy : 1.20.1 pytz : 2021.1 dateutil : 2.8.1 pip : 20.3.3 setuptools : 51.3.3 ```
comments:
not ideal but you can solve this with:
```
df.style.format(lambda x: f'{x:,.0f}' if isinstance(x, (float, int)) else '{x}').render()
```
there are few issues with `.to_html()`
Looks like a regression caused by #38759, don't think specific to `to_html`

review_comments: the expected html should be in a file, but I see #36690 slipped through https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/36690#discussion_r498745047 so OK to leave as follow-up
ok, thanks that's good to know. Will make a follow-up fixing that
